resolved_conflicts.explanation: The form ticks Public - State ownership, but its narrative describes a contract with the landowner and says the land title would revert to the original owners on abandonment. The structures remain state property under the contract, so the story describes both.

sources.title: Twinton Fire Lookout Tower, National Register of Historic Places Registration Form (NPS Form 10-900)

notes_for_editor: Build year and design come from the NRHP registration form, which says ca. 1933 in its description and 1933 in its period of significance. Two 2021 news items were tried: the Overton County News returned HTTP 429, and the Chattanoogan page had no readable text, so neither is cited. Some news coverage spells the maker Aeromotor; the form says Aermotor. Staffing, notable fires and public access are not in the sources. The form gives 80 ft total height; the record's 24.4 m matches that, but the form does not say whether it is to the cab floor, so no height fact was added. Ownership conflict is recorded in resolved_conflicts. Fact check 2026-10-09: the story gives the 1,863 ft figure as elevation, dates the build to around 1933 to match the form's ca. 1933, and drops the unsupported description of the current use as working.
